1.0 INTRODUCTION:

To ensure patient safety after the administration of medication creating a system for monitoring, reporting and analyzing the near misses, medication errors and adverse drug events.

2.0 SCOPE:

2.1 Hospital Wide – All Inpatient care areas

3.0 RESPONSIBILTY:

3.1 All Doctors

3.2 Nursing Staff

3.3 Pharmacist

4.0 ABBREVIATION:

4.1 NABH : National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare providers

4.2 MOM : Management of Medication

5.0 DEFINITION:

5.1 Near-miss:- A near-miss is an unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage--but had the potential to do so. Errors that did not result in patient harm, but could have, can be categorised as near-misses.

5.2 Adverse Drug Reactions: Adverse drug reaction (ADR) is any noxious, unintended, undesirable, or unexpected response to a drug that occurs at doses used in humans for prophylaxis, diagnosis, therapy of disease, or for modification of psychological function. This definition is understood to exclude predictable, dose-related side effects due to drugs which result in little or no change in Patient management, and in particular, mild extra pyramidal side effects due to neuroleptic drug therapy

5.3 Medication errors: A medication error is any preventable event that may cause or lead to inappropriate medication use or patient harm while the medication is in the control of the health care professional. Such events may be related professional practice, procedures, and systems, including prescribing; communication; labeling, packaging, and nomenclature; dispensing; distribution; administration; education; monitoring and use.

5.4 Types of errors: Order Error – Types of ordering errors include: inappropriate medication selected, inappropriate dose, illegible order, duplicate order, order not dated/timed, wrong patient/chart selected, contraindications, verbal order misunderstood, verbal order not written in the drug chart, wrong frequency, route, illegible writing, therapy duration, alert information bypassed or use of nonstandard nomenclature or abbreviations.

5.5 Transcription error –Transcription involves both the orders that are manually transcribed onto manual record (e.g. Drug chart). Types of transcription errors include: wrong medication, time, dose, frequency, duration, rate patient/chart, verbal order misunderstanding, verbal orders not entered into patient case sheet. 5.6 Preparation/Dispensing Error – Types of preparation and dispensing errors include: Inaccurate Labeling, wrong quantity, medication, dose, diluents, formulation, expired medication, refill error, and delay in medication delivery.

5.7Administration Error – Types of administration errors include: Wrong patient, dose, time, Medication, route, rate, extravagation (may be an ADR) and unauthorized dose given

5.8 Indications of adverse drug reactions: Indications of an ADR include anaphylaxis, arrhythmia, convulsions, hallucinations, shortness of breath, rashes, itching, hypotension, dystonia, leukopenia, urinary retention, symptoms associated with neuroleptic malignant syndrome, initial report of tardive dyskinesia, EPS related to non-antipsychotic drugs and also includes true allergic (hypersensitivity) reactions and idiosyncratic reactions.

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH : Accreditation Standards For Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS:-

7.1 Documented procedure exists to capture near miss, medication error and adverse drug event.

7.2 Near miss, medication error and adverse drug event are defined.

7.3 These are reported within a specified time frame.

7.4 They are collected and analyzed.

7.5 Corrective and/or preventive action(s) are taken based on the analysis where appropriate

8.0 PROCEDURES:

8.1 On notice of an unusual incident regarding a medication nursing staff are immediately report to the treating doctors and the Matron. A report is submitted to Pharmacy and Therapeutic committee. If the patient has sustained serious illness as a result of the incident, Risk Management must be notified. The medication error report includes:

1. Patient demographics (name, location, medical service);

2. Notation as to medical personnel who were notified of the incident (i.e. physician);

3. Severity rating of the incident;

4. Accurate description of incident.

All patients are monitored after medication administration by enquiring every patient or by documenting if the patient tells. The inpatients who are administered different drugs need monitoring during their stay in the hospital. Certain drugs can produce serious immediate or delayed side effects. Patients with past history of drug allergies are identified. If drugs prone to produce allergic reactions, it should be done with caution. A small dose of the drug is given and marked with time, if any drug allergy is noted the main dose administration is withheld and the doctor is informed. Drug reactions producing cardiac, neurological, pulmonary, skin etc. side effects are promptly identified and the concerned

Doctor are promptly informed and remedial action is taken. All events and actions taken are recorded by the concerned nurses in the patient’s case sheet and signed with date. The medical superintendent and the nursing superintendent or the nursing

supervisor are notified in cases where wrong medications are administered to a patient, or there has been negligence on the part of the nursing staff in following directions of drug administration and necessary investigations are initiated immediately. When Intra Venous (I.V) medications are given in presence of the nurse along with the patient to monitor the progress or note any undue side effects. Starting and discontinuation of I.V medication are done by the nurse and the details are noted in the case sheet with sign, date and time. The nurse are enquired about the patient’s welfare from time to time after such treatment and make sure that everything has been running smoothly. Adverse drug events are defined and the staff nurse who has administrated the drug will be reported to the doctor immediately and remedial actions will be taken, and before the shift, the concerned staff should fill the prescribed ADR forms available in all clinical areas. It should be given to the nursing superintendent through concerned nursing supervisor. Adverse drug events are collected and analyzed. Report and evaluate ADRs occurring in the concerned Pharmacy & therapeutic Committee meetings. These events are then be analyzed by the committee to identify probable cause and suggest and implement measures to prevent the same in future. Policies are modified to reduce adverse drug events when unacceptable trends occur. Labels, vials, packets of medicine due to which adverse event occurred are secured by on duty staff nurse and given to committee. Inform healthcare providers about ADRs to improve patient care.

8.2 Refer to MOM 5.0 definitions.

8.3 All adverse drug reactions are reported immediately to on duty doctors and to treating doctor within 10- 15 minutes and the interventions observed are documented in the patient case sheet. Same is reported to the pharmacy and therapeutic committee in a standardized format within 24 hours.

8.4 All adverse drug reactions are intensively analyzed by Pharmacy and Therapeutic committee and the corrective actions are taken based on the discussion in monthly audit meeting
